title: Efficacy of Conbercept in the Treatment of Choroidal Neovascularization Secondary to Pathologic Myopia

license.statement: CC BY (article <license>: 'Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY)'; no version or URL given in the licence element)

condition: Treatment-naive choroidal neovascularization secondary to pathologic myopia (refraction >= 6.0 D or axial length >= 26.0 mm; subfoveal 12 eyes, parafoveal 12 eyes); retrospective single-centre series (Zibo Central Hospital, September 2016 to June 2018), 24 eyes of 20 patients with at least 6 months of follow-up

groups.description: All eyes: one conbercept injection, further injections as needed (17 eyes received 1, 5 eyes 2 and 2 eyes 3 injections within 6 months)

notes: Time origin: the first intravitreal conbercept injection (treatment-naive eyes; prior intravitreal drugs and PDT excluded)
CRT measured on Optovue OCT and defined as the sum of the neurosensory retinal thickness and the subretinal fluid height, without a subfield or point definition, so measure central_unspecified
Regimen: single initial injection then as-needed reinjection (no loading), regimen prn
